novel_features.name: Device topology tree
novel_features.description: See the physical device tree (gateway to switches to APs) built entirely from local mirror data, no live crawl needed.
novel_features.rationale: Requires joining devices and uplink/port data locally into a tree; no single endpoint returns hierarchy.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this when an agent needs to understand physical network layout without walking every device endpoint individually.

novel_features.name: Config drift detection
novel_features.description: Show what changed in site config (networks, firewall, wifi, DNS) since the last sync snapshot.
novel_features.rationale: Requires comparing two local snapshots taken at different sync times; the API has no versioning or audit trail.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use after a suspected config change to see exactly what moved, without manually diffing the controller UI.

novel_features.name: Newcomer detection
novel_features.description: List devices and clients first seen since a given sync, for spotting new hardware joining the network.
novel_features.rationale: Requires a local snapshot diff of the devices and clients tables; the API has no since filter.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use for periodic security review of what joined the network recently.

novel_features.name: Port audit
novel_features.description: Review port utilization and PoE status across every switch on a site in one table.
novel_features.rationale: Requires joining device port config with local topology and PoE/link data across all switches; no endpoint aggregates this.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use before adding new PoE devices to check headroom, or to find unused ports across a stack.

novel_features.name: Guest network report
novel_features.description: Summarize guest network usage: active vouchers and connected guest clients, from local data.
novel_features.rationale: Requires joining hotspot vouchers, guest WiFi broadcasts, and guest client sessions from the local store; no combined endpoint exists.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use for a quick guest-network health check without cross-referencing three separate UI screens.

novel_features.name: Firewall rule prediction
novel_features.description: Predict which firewall policy would match a hypothetical packet before making a live change.
novel_features.rationale: Requires locally replaying firewall zone/policy/ACL/traffic-matching-list evaluation order; the API has no trace/simulate endpoint.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use to check the effect of a proposed firewall change before applying it live.

narrative.headline: Every UniFi Network API operation, plus drift detection, topology, and rule prediction no other UniFi tool has.
narrative.value_prop: unifi-pp-cli wraps the full local Network integration API (devices, clients, firewall, ACL, networks, VPN, switching) with a local SQLite mirror. That mirror is what lets it answer questions the live API can't: what changed since yesterday, what device just joined, and which firewall rule would match a given packet.
narrative.auth_narrative: Generate a local API key from the gateway's own UI (Settings -> Control Plane -> Integrations -> Create API Key) and set UNIFI_API_KEY. The gateway's self-signed certificate is handled automatically for private/loopback/link-local hosts; no --insecure flag needed for the common case.

quickstart.comment: Confirm config and connectivity without making a live call.
Find the site ID you'll use for every other command.
Populate the local mirror so drift/topology/newcomer have a baseline.
Check what changed in the last day.

troubleshoots.symptom: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority
troubleshoots.fix: This should auto-resolve for private/loopback/link-local gateway hosts; if your gateway is reachable via a public hostname, set UNIFI_INSECURE_SKIP_VERIFY=1 explicitly.
Regenerate the API key under Settings -> Control Plane -> Integrations on the gateway and re-export UNIFI_API_KEY.
Run 'unifi-pp-cli sync' first to populate the local mirror; these commands are local-mirror-only.

narrative.when_to_use: Use this CLI for scripted or agent-driven UniFi Network audits, firewall/ACL review, and change-detection on a self-hosted gateway. Best for homelab/prosumer operators who want terminal-first control instead of the web UI.
anti_triggers: Do not use this for UniFi Protect (cameras) or UniFi Access (doors) — this CLI only covers the Network integration API.
Do not use this for the legacy cloud/CloudKey Controller API — that's a different auth model entirely.
Do not treat rule-predict's output as a live-gateway guarantee — it simulates against the last synced ruleset.
